method: Read the exe bytes (original/game/cataclysm.exe, PE sections parsed in Python) plus the Ghidra exports. ShipTypeToStr (CET 0x4D6BC0) led to the shiptypeinfo name table; InitStatShipInfo (found via its index into PTR_DAT_008b1938) copies 0x23 dwords from shipHeaders[type] into ShipStaticInfo+0x108, which fixes the Cataclysm CustShipHeader at 0x8C bytes: sizeofShipSpecifics + 34 function slots, no leading shiptype field. Every slot read through ship->staticinfo (+0x20) was located with objdump (mov reg,[x+0x20]; mov reg,[reg+0x10C..0x190]; call reg) and each call site was matched to its HW1 caller (InitStatShipInfo, univCreateShip, univFreeShipContents, processSpecialToDo, univDeleteDeadShip, SaveShip/LoadShip/FixShip, ShipSelect checks, clHalt/clDock/move). The 51 distinct headers were attributed to modules by the ship types that use them, the alphabetical object-file order of .data/.text, the per-module script-key strings and debug strings, and by comparing each header non-NULL slot set with the HW1 initializers parsed from HomeworldSDL/src/Ships/*.c (exact matches for GravWellGenerator, MissileDestroyer, GenericInterceptor, AttackBomber, CloakedFighter, ProximitySensor, IonCannonFrigate, etc.). Functions are named <Module><Slot> (HW1 names verbatim where HW1 had that slot). Only 72 of the 324 distinct slot targets are Ghidra functions; the other 252 are listed in the run summary, not proposed. Shared addresses are identical-code folds (a RET stub 0x49AE30, a return-0 stub 0x6FE9A0 and the return-1 stub 0x497DB0, which missions.json names kasfSpecialOff, carry many slots); 0x497DB0 is left to that file.
